plain_description.what: On the multi-corpus routing data, sends low-confidence or out-of-scope questions to the best single model instead of the per-cell routed model. The tree is built separately within each source benchmark, so it is source-conditioned, not fully label-free. It compares this with escalating the same share of questions at random, with a k-means version beside it. No judge calls.
plain_description.why: It checks whether route confidence (margin, out-of-scope detection) is a usable safety valve for the routing product.
plain_description.information: If confidence-based escalation beats random escalation, the router knows when it is unsure. If it loses, the confidence signal is misleading. Result: done, undetermined. It beats random escalation by +0.50pp, but the interval just touches zero (a boundary case, below the detectable effect size). Compared with no escalation it adds almost nothing (+0.15pp). It avoids the cost of random escalation but buys almost no accuracy. The failure condition did not fire.
